questions.question: The length of an IPv6 address is
questions.explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits long, which is not among options A-C. 32 bits is the IPv4 address length.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to extract or filter the data & information from the data warehouse?
questions.explanation: Data mining extracts useful patterns and information from data warehouses. A data recovery tool restores lost data, so 'Both B and C' is wrong.

questions.question: In a balanced binary tree, the height of two sub-trees of every node can not differ by more than

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In a height-balanced (AVL) tree, the heights of the left and right subtrees of every node differ by at most 1.

questions.question: What is a socket in the context of process-to-process communication?

options.A: A hardware device for data transmission
options.B: A software interface for network communication
options.C: A type of cable used for high-speed data transmission

questions.explanation: A socket is a software endpoint (IP address plus port) through which processes communicate over a network. It is not hardware, a cable or a topology.

questions.question: In a relational database, what is a primary key?

options.A: A key used for opening encrypted data
options.B: A unique identifier for a record in a table
options.C: A foreign key from another table

questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each record (row) in a table and cannot be null. A foreign key references another table's key, and an index is a separate access structure.

questions.question: The term "FAT" stands for:
questions.explanation: FAT stands for File Allocation Table, a table that records which clusters belong to each file on the disk. It is a table, not a tree or graph.

questions.question: Process-to-process communication involves communication between:

options.B: Different devices on the same network

questions.explanation: Process-to-process communication, provided by the transport layer using port numbers, is between application processes running on different hosts. Host-to-host delivery between devices is the network layer's job.

questions.question: Conditional asymptotic notation allows for a more nuanced analysis of algorithm behavior under specific conditions. This is particularly useful when:

options.A: Analyzing algorithms with constant time complexity
options.D: Algorithm behavior varies based on certain input characteristics

questions.explanation: Conditional asymptotic notation states a bound that holds only when the input satisfies some condition (for example n is a power of 2), so it is useful when behaviour depends on input characteristics. Constant-time or fixed-size cases need no such condition.

questions.question: Which programming paradigm focuses on breaking down a program into smaller procedures or functions?
questions.explanation: Procedural programming structures a program as a sequence of procedures or functions. OOP organizes code around objects, and functional programming around pure functions.

questions.question: Which among the following search algorithms requires the least memory?
questions.explanation: DFS stores only the current path and unexplored siblings, giving O(bm) space, while BFS must keep the whole frontier, O(b^d). So DFS uses the least memory among the AI search strategies.

questions.question: "Ctrl + Page Down" is used to

options.A: move the cursor one paragraph down
options.B: move the cursor one page down
options.C: move the cursor one line down
options.D: move the cursor one screen down

questions.explanation: In Word, Ctrl+Page Down moves the cursor to the top of the next page. Page Down alone moves one screen down.

questions.question: An assembly language is a/an

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Assembly language uses mnemonics that map almost one-to-one to machine instructions, so it is a low-level language. C is often called middle-level, not assembly.

questions.question: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets, used to style HTML documents. The other expansions are incorrect.

questions.question: _____ clause creates temporary relation for the query on which it is defined.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The WITH clause defines a temporary relation (common table expression) that exists only for the query in which it is defined.

questions.question: ___________ is basically a form of pictorial presentation.
questions.explanation: Animation is a form of pictorial presentation in which a sequence of images creates the illusion of motion. Photography and drawing are static images and creativity is not a medium.

questions.question: Which data structure is used for efficient searching, insertion, and deletion of elements?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A hash table supports search, insertion and deletion in O(1) average time. Stacks and queues only give efficient access at their ends, and searching them is O(n).

questions.question: What is a PLA?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: PLA stands for Programmable Logic Array, a PLD with programmable AND and OR planes.

questions.question: Which of the following can improve the performance of AI agent?
questions.explanation: Learning lets an agent improve its performance from experience. Precision and observing alone do not improve performance, so 'All of the above' is wrong.

questions.question: What are abstract methods?

options.A: Methods that are inaccessible to the outside world
options.C: Methods without a body, defined in an abstract class

questions.explanation: An abstract method is declared without a body in an abstract class (or interface) and must be implemented by subclasses. Methods with implementation are concrete methods.

questions.question: "Ctrl + Page Up" is used to

options.A: move the cursor one page up
options.B: move the cursor one paragraph up
options.C: move the cursor one screen up
options.D: move the cursor one line up

questions.explanation: In Word, Ctrl+Page Up moves the cursor to the top of the previous page. Page Up alone moves one screen up.

questions.question: Among the following, which statement is correct about the modularity?

options.A: Modularity means hiding the parts of the program.
options.B: Modularity refers to dividing a program into subsequent small modules or independent parts.
options.C: It refers to overloading the program's part.
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Modularity means dividing a program into smaller, independent modules. Hiding parts of the program describes abstraction/data hiding.

questions.question: Communication between a computer and a keyboard involves _____ transmission.

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Data flows only from the keyboard to the computer, which is simplex (one-way) transmission.

questions.question: Which one of the following would breach the integrity of a system?

options.A: Locking the room to prevent theft
options.B: Full access rights for all users
options.C: Fitting the system with an anti-theft device
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Giving full access rights to all users allows anyone to modify data, which breaches integrity. Locking rooms and anti-theft devices improve physical security.

questions.question: Which type of register is primarily used to temporarily hold data during arithmetic and logical operations in a microprocessor?
questions.explanation: The accumulator holds one operand and the intermediate result of arithmetic and logical operations performed by the ALU. Shift and counter registers have specialised roles, not general operand storage.

questions.question: Safeguards in an operating system are mechanisms used to:

options.A: Ensure the efficient utilization of CPU time
options.B: Prevent data loss during power outages
options.C: Enhance the performance of I/O operations
options.D: Protect against unauthorized access and security breaches

questions.explanation: OS safeguards (authentication, access control, protection) are mechanisms that protect the system against unauthorized access and security breaches.
